source.method: Real Stage 2 geometry, orthographic elevations. Straight street panels meet at matching edges; each curved turn is a separate wider view. The winding 3D route is unfolded in travel order, so turn boundaries are intentional perspective transitions. Alley supplements use oblique overhead views to expose the courts behind street façades.

districts.title: the Mouth
districts.note: Sanjō Ōhashi, a hidden tunnel roji, and the first shops of rakuchū

districts.title: the Alley Maze
districts.note: yuka river decks, narrow geiko zushi, vine trellises and crooked ridges

districts.title: the Water Maze
districts.note: two cargo takasebune, willow fronds, bridge culverts and cherry boughs

districts.title: the Long Canopy
districts.note: Teramachi lanterns, stained-glass vaults, rafter catwalks and skylights

districts.title: Laundry Sky
districts.note: drying decks, folks hanging yukata, tunnel lanes, futons and high cisterns

districts.title: Festival Streets
districts.note: bustling yatai stalls, folding screens, a kakiyama and the great hoko float

districts.title: the Sending Fires
districts.note: five fires on the Kyoto hills, across the roofs you ran
